receipt.question: On Motion to Suspend the Rules and Pass

finding.text: On May 20, 2026, Valerie Foushee voted Yea on passing S.2393, which would authorize a St. Louis VA bed tower and clinical expansion, together with administrative, warehouse, utility and parking construction, at a maximum project amount of $1,762,668,000. The bill separately authorizes appropriations for fiscal year 2026 or the year funds are appropriated. It does not itself appropriate the money or establish that construction or care was delivered.

qualifications.text: This interpretation concerns the House suspension-and-passage vote on the Senate-engrossed text, not a claim of enactment. The bill’s printed short title says fiscal year 2025, while its operative project and appropriation-authorization provisions say fiscal year 2026. The project combines clinical and nonclinical construction. The vote establishes no general veteran benefit, patient-admission rule, guaranteed construction date, or medical outcome. No motive or preferred alternative is inferred.

scope_label.text: One reviewed vote on a St. Louis VA facility authorization. This is a bounded sample, not an assessment of the member’s overall Health record.

presentations.coverage_text: This conclusion covers 7 reviewed substantive actions across 5 independent policy episodes in the 119th Congress.
presentations.scope_boundary: This conclusion remains bounded to the reviewed 119th-Congress sample.

conclusion.headline: A divide by policy mechanism in the reviewed sample
conclusion.body: In this reviewed 119th-Congress sample, Foushee supported reporting and evidence, research, or implementation conditions in two independent episodes, while opposing three specific proposals concerning retired-service firearm access, broader D.C. police pursuit authority, and repeal of most reviewed D.C. policing restrictions.

repeated_patterns.heading: Certification, fentanyl research provisions, and officer-safety reporting
repeated_patterns.body: Across independent episodes, Foushee supported an overdose-reduction certification condition, a later fentanyl framework with research provisions, and officer-safety reporting requirements.

repeated_patterns.heading: Retired-service firearm access, D.C. pursuit authority, and policing-rule rollbacks
repeated_patterns.body: Across independent episodes, Foushee opposed creating a reviewed federal program for eligible current and retired officers to buy qualifying retired agency firearms, broader D.C. police pursuit authority, and repeal of most reviewed D.C. policing restrictions.

policy_trajectories.heading: The fentanyl episode is mixed
policy_trajectories.body: Within one fentanyl legislative episode, Foushee supported a certification amendment, opposed the earlier House bill, and supported a later related framework that permanently scheduled fentanyl-related substances and included research provisions. These related stages count as one episode for breadth and do not establish a change in position, motive, or philosophy.
